title: Component (friction block) manifest
description: A component is NOT a model: it has no equilibrium, no welfare and no verification tier of its own, so manifest.schema.json cannot describe it honestly. The fields that make composition checkable are provides, requires and replaces.

kind.description: assumption = a maintained assumption that friction blocks replace (it has no friction parameter); core = the skeleton other blocks mount on

friction.description: One line: the friction introduced. Omitted for kind=core and kind=assumption.

provides.description: Endogenous variables this component introduces. Names must exist in taxonomy/variables.yaml.

requires.description: Variables used but introduced elsewhere. Composition fails if no included component provides one.

normalisation.description: e.g. 'one unit', 'one standard deviation', '25 basis points annualised'

prior.description: Required when method = estimated. The largest omission of the current model manifest.

formula.description: Required when method = derived: how the parameter is built from others.

id.description: Unique within the component. Referenced as <component-id>.<equation-id> by `replaces`.

expr.description: Linear expression equal to zero. x(+1) is a lead, x(-1) a lag, x the current value.

source.description: Equation number in the cited article.

replaces.description: Fully qualified equation ids this component removes, e.g. core-nk-classical.flex-price-output. Two included components replacing the same equation is a composition error.

depends_on.description: Component ids that must also be included (indexation blocks modify another block rather than standing alone).

minimum_perturbation_order.description: Recursive preferences and stochastic volatility have no effect at first order. A block solved below its required order runs and means nothing.

nesting_target.description: The verification analogue of reproduces_paper for a block that has no paper of its own: at this parameter limit the block must vanish and the composed model must reproduce the core's own numbers.

recovers.description: The composition (without this block) whose solution must be recovered.

pathological.description: True when the limit is a degenerate case rather than a valid nesting test (e.g. soe-closure, whose limit reintroduces a unit root).
